chapter: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
title: First recordings with Cuarteto Caney, Cugat and Noro Morales
summary: Alfredito Valdes gave him his first recording break with Cuarteto Caney; he freelanced with Noro Morales, Cugat and Augusto Coen and played in Orquesta Siboney.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: At La Conga. When he came to Havana Madrid he played about two or three years or four and then from there we went to La Conga. We worked together, we made a recording, as a matter of fact, he was the first one to give me the break, to sing on recording, so we sing together with Caney, Cuarteto Caney.
they were here, that's when Socarras got the offer to go with La Anacaona.
The all-girl jazz band, La Anacaona.
And that didn't occur until the following year, thirty-nine. Right. Okay. So I know that you recorded and worked with Noro Morales, Xavier Cugat, Caney and.....

....Augusto Coen, and you recorded with them then. I just forgot the order that it goes in ahh, but I gather that you must have been very big to work with these bands because they were the top bands of the day. Now here you weren't singing for a while and bang, you come back into it and you start making recordings and working. Ahh, according to what they sent me from Finland, you recorded Cachita in 1940 with Xavier Cugat. I forgot the date, it was January something, January 14, 1940.
You were just free-lancing then, Macho?
Yes, even that I was working with Orquesta Siboney, early part of 1940.
And then I recorded with Noro, with everyone. I was free-lancing with everyone.
